Rahul Gandhi participates in a conversation with journalist Lydia Polgreen during an open Q&A session at Columbia University on November 17, 2026. (Photo: X/@INCIndia)
The Bharatiya Janata Party on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) accused the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, of persistently attempting to defame India on foreign soil and undermining the country’s global standing.
“Continuing this trend, he once again made false, baseless and unfounded statements at Columbia University in the United States. The entire nation and every Indian feels ashamed that the Leader of the Opposition speaks against India in this manner on foreign soil,” BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said at a press conference.
Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University on Tuesday, Mr. Gandhi had said that India was sitting on an “economic disaster” that could become far more serious if the country continued on its present course.
Countering Mr. Gandhi’s claims, Mr. Bhatia said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, India was scaling new heights in democracy, economy, youth power, and global standing. Its internal strength and international identity has been bolstered, the BJP spokesperson claimed.
“On the other hand, Rahul Gandhi has become a symbol of anarchy, immaturity and hatred towards India. He travels abroad and makes false statements to undermine India’s progress and its strengthening global image. His actions expose his anti-India mindset,” Mr. Bhatia said, describing Mr. Gandhi as a “habitual offender”.
The BJP leader added: “His intention is to weaken the strong and stable government that has been in power in India for the past 12 years.”
He said that while Mr. Gandhi claims that India is on the verge of an economic disaster, data showed that the country recorded real GDP growth of 7.8% from April to June 2026. “On October 26, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projected growth of 7% for the Indian economy in FY 2027. India is recording the fastest growth among the world’s major economies,” he said, adding that the IMF had projected growth of 4.4% for China and 2.3% for the U.S.
Mr. Bhatia further said that 65% of India’s population was below the age of 35, and described this as the country’s “greatest asset and demographic strength”. He added that the younger generation saw a bright future for itself.
India’s unemployment rate had declined from 5% to 4.9% in October 2026, while the labour force participation rate had increased to 55.7%, primarily driven by the growing participation of women in the workforce, he said. On private investment, Mr. Bhatia said the latest figures showed quarterly growth of 11.9%, “perhaps the highest in the world”.
He claimed that Mr. Gandhi had described the Indian media as weak and biased, but in reality, the BJP leader said, it was “a strong fourth pillar of democracy that brings the views of both the ruling party and the Opposition before the public”.
Mr. Bhatia also alleged that the Congress leader had “repeatedly raised doubts about the fairness of elections in India and the role of the Election Commission of India” without any basis.
